title: Overhaul Test Suites to 30s Budget Per App
description: Every project's default `test` nx target must finish in ≤30s (Rust measured as warm-cache test execution, compile excluded). Structurally slow suites (Storybook/Playwright e2e, Postgres testcontainer tests in compose/server/hub/rs/bin.rs, VSCode extension-host suite) move to a separate opt-in `test-e2e` target excluded from the default test run. Add a central hard wall-clock guard in repo/lib/js/index.ts so runner helpers (vitest, cargo, pytest, go, dotnet, bun test) enforce the budget and fail loudly on regression. Trim tests across all ~90 projects to keep only complicated-feature coverage (algorithms, geometry, protocol, interaction/reducer logic) and delete trivial tests (export-exists checks, getter identity, CSS-substring matching, serde round-trip padding). Execute via a fleet of parallel agents, one per project, each measuring baseline, trimming, migrating to the budgeted helper, and verifying ≤30s.
summary:
Fixed mathematical/number's `primes::tests::long::factor_natural_random_semiprime`, which was hanging indefinitely (didn't finish in 22min CPU-bound) instead of meeting the 30s budget.

Root cause: the test factored a semiprime of two *balanced* ~60-bit primes (p=1000000000000000003, q=999999999999999989), forcing `pollard_rho_natural` down its Pollard-rho path with an expected ~sqrt(2^60)≈2^30 (~1 billion) iterations — mathematically infeasible for this algorithm regardless of implementation quality, consistent with `factor()`'s own docstring that hard balanced semiprimes are out of scope (no ECM/QS here). Confirmed via `git log`/blame that this was pre-existing and unrelated to a same-file clippy-only cleanup pass.

Two changes in mathematical/number/rs/src/primes.rs:
1. `pollard_rho_natural` was computing a full arbitrary-precision GCD on every single Floyd-cycle iteration, unlike its `pollard_rho_u64` sibling which batches GCDs every 128 steps (Brent-style). Rewrote it to batch identically (with a single-step backtrack fallback on batch overshoot), removing an unnecessary and inconsistent per-iteration cost — a real inefficiency independent of the test-sizing issue.
2. Changed the test's second factor from a ~60-bit prime to 104,729 (the 10,000th prime, already used elsewhere in this file) — still forces the >64-bit `Natural` code path (product is ~77 bits) and genuinely exercises `pollard_rho_natural`, but now converges in ~1,000 iterations instead of ~1 billion.

Verified: `cargo test -p mathematical_number --release` (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/some-dir) — all 79 tests pass in 0.01s (finished in 0.00s. Prior CPU-bound the whole time.
Also ran `cargo clippy -p mathematical_number --release --all-targets` — clean, no warnings.
